Repo: /Users/maya/nextjs-ecommerce — a Next.js 14 storefront using App Router, server components, and React Server Components for dynamic product rendering.

Task: design

We’re seeing hydration mismatches on the product listing page in production, particularly when filtering by category. The client sometimes re-renders everything even when only the query param changes. We suspect it’s related to how we’re using `useRouter` state vs. React state to manage filters.

Below is the full component tree and a snippet from a Sentry log showing a hydration error:

```
Component Hierarchy:
- app/products/page.tsx (async)
  - ProductFilterBar (client component)
    - CategoryFilterDropdown (client)
    - PriceRangeFilter (client)
  - ProductGrid (server component)
    - ProductCard (client)

Error: Hydration failed because the initial UI does not match what was rendered on the server
  at <ProductGrid> (at page.tsx:45:7)
  at <div> (at ProductFilterBar.tsx:12:3)
  at <ProductFilterBar> (at page.tsx:40:5)

React caught an error thrown during render.
```

Also pasting a long comment thread from an internal Slack thread about this:

> @frontend @infra — we’ve had 3 P0 incidents in the past week tied to RSC hydration flakes. The product listing page is especially flaky when filters are applied quickly. We’ve tried `use client` everywhere, but that defeats the benefit of RSCs. One theory: we’re mixing router state and local state in a way that causes server and client to diverge.
>
> I noticed that `ProductFilterBar` maintains filter state in React (`const [category, setCategory]`) but also updates the URL via `router.push`. Could this be causing a mismatch between what the server thinks the filters are and what the client renders?
>
> Another thought: should we be using `useEffect` to sync state with the URL, or rely entirely on searchParams in server components? The docs say server components should derive state from params, but we’re passing filter state down to client components as props, which might be stale.
>
> Also, we’re not using `refresh` or `replace` correctly? Sometimes the back button doesn’t restore previous filter state.
>
> Related: https://github.com/vercel/next.js/issues/49220 — 'RSC + client component state divergence when using useRouter'
>
> One proposed fix: move all filter state into URL searchParams and let the server component re-render based on that. But that would trigger full RSC re-render on every change — slower UX?
>
> Alternative: use React state in the client component but pass a `key` prop to `ProductGrid` that includes filter state, forcing a fresh server render. But that might break streaming.
>
> Another idea: use SWR or a state sync library like Zustand to keep client and server in sync? But that adds complexity and defeats RSCs.

Given this context, design a solution that avoids hydration mismatches while preserving RSC benefits. Argue for one architecture over others, citing trade-offs in DX, performance, and correctness. Your answer must include:
- A proposed component structure and state management strategy
- A comparison of at least three alternatives (e.g. full URL state, local state + key invalidation, client-side hydration sync)
- A precise definition of how to test for correctness in CI
- A discussion of how this approach scales if we add sorting, search, and pagination

We’re building a real-time collaboration feature in a Next.js app at /Users/sam/project-board — it’s a kanban board with drag-and-drop powered by `react-beautiful-dnd`, now adding multi-user sync via WebSockets.

The current architecture uses a client-side WebSocket connection to push updates, but we’re seeing race conditions when two users move the same card. The UI gets out of sync, and optimistic updates don’t roll back cleanly.

Pasted from a long Sentry trace and dev log:

> [WebSocket] Received conflicting update for card "C-123":
>   - Client A: PATCH /cards/C-123 { listId: "WIP", position: 2 }
>   - Client B: PATCH /cards/C-123 { listId: "Review", position: 1 }
>   → Server applied B, but A still shows it in WIP
>
> We tried queueing client updates and reapplying on conflict, but `react-beautiful-dnd` doesn’t support async drag end.
>
> One idea: use CRDTs (like Automerge) to merge updates without server coordination. But we don’t want to send full document state on every change.
>
> Another: sequence numbers or Lamport timestamps on updates. But clock skew is a problem.
>
> We’re also using Zustand for local state, but it’s not shared or serialized.
>
> Related: https://github.com/atlassian/react-beautiful-dnd/issues/1819 — 'Support for optimistic updates and conflict resolution'
>
> Some teams use a "last write wins" policy, but that’s bad for UX — users don’t know their change was ignored.
>
> We tried operational transforms (OT), but it’s complex for drag-and-drop with nested structure (lists, cards, positions).
>
> One more: move all drag events through a central queue with server-side conflict resolution and broadcast. But that adds latency.
>
> We’re not using Redis or Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY yet — should we?
>
> Also, do we need to support offline editing?

Design a real-time sync strategy for drag-and-drop that ensures consistency and resolves conflicts gracefully. Your answer must:
- Propose a concrete data model for card and list state (e.g. with version vectors, timestamps, or positions)
- Compare at least three conflict resolution strategies (e.g. last write wins, OT, CRDT, manual merge)
- Explain how optimistic updates are handled and rolled back if rejected
- Describe how the UI indicates sync status and conflicts
- Argue for one architecture, including trade-offs in latency, consistency, and complexity

Repo: /Users/tina/nextjs-blog — a markdown blog using Next.js 14, `app/content/posts/`, and `remark` for MDX parsing.

Task: design

We want to add search with full-text indexing. The site has ~500 posts, all static. We don’t want to add a backend or use Algolia.

We’re considering client-side search with `lunr.js`, but it bundles the entire index in JS — bad for perf.

Pasted from a GitHub issue thread:

> We tried `lunr` with a generated `search-index.json` file. The bundle size went from 40KB to 1.2MB. Lighthouse says "page unresponsive for 2.3s on low-end devices."
>
> Alternative: use `flexsearch` — smaller footprint, but still requires loading 10MB of text in memory to index.
>
> Another: split index by year or tag? But then search is fragmented.
>
> One team used `@orama/orama` — tree-shakable, lazy-loads index chunks. But it’s beta.
>
> What if we precompute TF-IDF scores and only send top N terms per document?
>
> Or use a Web Worker to avoid blocking main thread?
>
> Another idea: use `createStaticHandler` to serve a `/api/search?q=` endpoint that returns filtered results from a prebuilt JSON index. But that requires JS to be enabled.
>
> Related: https://github.com/nextjs/next.js/discussions/50921 — 'Static site search without external service'
>
> One person suggested using `next build` to generate a `search-index.mjs` module that’s dynamically imported. But that still loads all data.
>
> What about streaming the index in chunks and indexing incrementally?
>
> Also, should we support fuzzy search? Stemming? Accents? The blog has Spanish and French posts.

Design a full-text search solution that balances bundle size, search quality, and build time. Your answer must:
- Propose a concrete architecture (e.g. prebuilt index format, loading strategy, client/server balance)
- Compare at least three approaches (e.g. client-only, hybrid API + partial index, pure server-side)
- Explain how it handles i18n and special characters
- Define what "acceptable" bundle size and TTFB means for this site
- Argue for one solution with trade-offs in DX, UX, and scalability

In the repo at /Users/developer/game-engine-repo, we need to modify the `PhysicsSystem::update` method in src/physics/physics_system.cpp to ensure that collision detection runs *before* any movement updates. Right now, objects are being moved and then checked for collisions, which can lead to tunneling issues. We want to reorder the logic inside the update loop so that all collision shapes are swept and tested prior to applying velocities.

"We've been seeing consistent reports from QA about fast-moving projectiles passing through thin walls. The issue only happens at high speeds, suggesting a lack of continuous collision detection or incorrect update ordering. After some profiling, I noticed that our current update sequence applies velocity first, then checks for overlaps. This is backwards. The design doc below explicitly states the correct order: "All rigid bodies must have their potential paths evaluated for intersection before any transformation is committed." We should follow that."

"Additionally, the engine spec from 2021 (quoted below) says:

> The physics tick is divided into phases: (1) integration of forces, (2) broad-phase collision culling, (3) narrow-phase collision detection, (4) resolution and impulse application. No phase shall proceed to the next object until the current object has completed the phase. Movement without prior collision prediction violates this invariant.

This was brought up during sprint retro last week and needs to be fixed before alpha release. Make the minimal necessary change to enforce correct phase ordering. Do not rewrite the entire system—just restructure the existing loop. Read the file first, confirm current behavior, then make the edit.

Edit src/graphics/shader_manager.cpp to fix a crash when reloading shaders during runtime. The issue occurs when calling `ShaderManager::reloadAll()` while the game is paused but renderables still exist. We get a null pointer dereference in `applyUniforms()` because the program ID is zero after reload.

"I added debug logs and traced it to this sequence:

- User presses F5 to reload shaders
- ShaderManager deletes old GL program IDs and compiles new ones
- But some MeshRenderer instances still hold stale pointers to the old Program object
- When the next frame renders (even if paused), applyUniforms() tries to use program->id, which is now invalid

This doesn't happen on startup because everything is synchronized. It only happens on hot reload."

"From the engine documentation:

> ShaderManager owns all compiled shader programs. Clients must not cache Program* beyond the scope of a single frame unless they subscribe to the onShaderReloaded event. All renderable components that bind shaders must re-acquire their Program reference after a reload notification.

We aren't using the event system here. The MeshRenderer class currently caches a raw pointer to Program in its setup() method but never refreshes it. Update ShaderManager::reloadAll() to emit a signal (use the existing EventBroker singleton) and modify MeshRenderer to listen and clear its cached Program pointer when that fires. Then force a rebind next draw. Keep the change focused—only touch the reload logic and MeshRenderer’s shader handling.

Fix a bug in src/audio/sound_fader.cpp where fading out a sound channel doesn’t stop playback when volume hits zero. Currently, the fade function decreases amplitude over time but leaves the channel running indefinitely.

"QA submitted this transcript:

> Step 1: Play sound with channel->fadeIn(2.0f, 1.0f);
> Step 2: Call channel->fadeOut(1.0f);
> Expected: Sound stops playing completely at end of fade
> Actual: Sound continues playing silently; channel remains occupied
> Impact: Only 32 channels available — we run out quickly

Logs show the internal m_volume reaches 0.0 but isStillPlaying() returns true until manually stopped."

"The original design notes from 2019 say:

> Fading out a channel should automatically invoke stop() once the target gain reaches zero, unless the fade type is cyclic. This ensures efficient resource usage and prevents orphaned channels.

Cyclic fades are rare and marked explicitly via setFadeMode(). Current code doesn’t check this. Add logic to SoundChannel::update() so that when a fade completes normally (not canceled), and fade mode is not cyclic, it calls stop() internally. Do not modify public API. Just fix the automatic cleanup.

"""
PERIOD STATE LIFECYCLE

States: DRAFT → OPEN → CLOSING → CLOSED → ARCHIVED

Allowed transitions:
- DRAFT → OPEN (on first invoice generation)
- OPEN → CLOSING (manual trigger or EOM)
- CLOSING → CLOSED (after final validations)
- CLOSED → ARCHIVED (after 30 days)

Any transition to CLOSED must be idempotent — multiple closure attempts should succeed silently if already CLOSED.

Idempotency note: closePeriod(String) should check current state first. If already CLOSED or beyond, return early without error.
"""
